Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the SIG package you sent last week. Medico Health's security team is working through the BCP/Disaster Recovery section and we had a couple of clarifying questions before we mark items as "complete" on our side. Short list below — can you confirm by EOD Tuesday if possible?

1) RTO/RPO: The SIG asks for documented RTO and RPO for production API endpoints and for customer data restore. Can you provide the numbers and any measured evidence?
2) Backups: Frequency, retention, and whether backups are stored cross-region or only within the same cloud region.
3) Failover: High level of the automated cross-region failover sequence and estimated time-to-service during failover (including DNS/traffic cutover).
4) Last test: Date of most recent DR test and whether a test report is available.

We can accept short answers + pointers to artifacts (runbook, test report, recorded session). I'm copying our ops partner Marco in case we need to coordinate a technical call.

Thanks — Claire

Hi Claire —

Appreciate the clear list. Answers below; I included attachments with short summaries and screenshots. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call if you want to walk through any of this.

1) RTO / RPO (production API endpoints & data):
- RTO (API endpoints): 20 minutes for regional failover to warm standby under standard load; 25-30 minutes observed under sustained high traffic during our last measured run.
- RPO (customer data): < 5 minutes for transactional data (log-structured replication + WAL shipping); overnight archive retention is configurable per account.
- Evidence: see attached redwood_SIG_bcp_summary_20270912.pdf (section 2) — contains timings measured in our 2027-06-09 drill.

2) Backups:
- Snapshot cadence: incremental snapshots every 5 minutes for critical state (KV/cache checkpointing where applicable) and full snapshots nightly.
- Retention: default 30 days; configurable to 90/365 days under enterprise settings.
- Storage: backups are written to customer-specified cloud object storage and replicated to a secondary region (cross-region replication enabled by default for hosted accounts). Screenshots: backup-config-screenshots.png attached.

3) Automated failover sequence (high level):
- Detect: health checks + latency thresholds trigger automated failover policy.
- Promote: warm-standby fleet in target region is promoted; model weights and KV caches are warmed using pre-shared snapshot and prefix cache.
- Traffic cutover: we rely on traffic routing via our smart router + DNS TTLs; expected DNS propagation + router convergence completes within 10-15 minutes in normal conditions.
- Total expected time-to-service: 20 minutes typical; 25-35 minutes under load (includes cache warm-up).

4) Last test + artifacts:
- Most recent full DR drill: 2027-06-09 (controlled failover from us-west1 -> us-east4).
- Test artifacts: redwood_SIG_bcp_summary_20270912.pdf (test log + RTO/RPO measurements), redwood_dr_runbook_v3.pdf (runbook). We have a short recording of the exercise: https://drive.google.com/recordings/dr-drill-20270609

Attachments: [redwood_SIG_bcp_summary_20270912.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)], [backup-config-screenshots.png (PNG, 420KB)], [redwood_dr_runbook_v3.pdf (PDF, 850KB)]

Next steps: if you need specific logs/tests for particular accounts under Medico's tenancy, let us know the account IDs and we can pull scoped evidence.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Reliability
